newsitem.title: USA: HemoCleanse gets FDA approval for study.
newsitem.headline: HemoCleanse gets FDA approval for study.

text.p: HemoCleanse Inc said Monday its BioLogic-HT System was approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for use in a feasibility study.
The study involves extracorporeal whole-body hyperthermia (WBH) treatment of metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
WBH involves elevating the body temperature to control or destroy viruses and other heat sensitive organisms. The study will be conducted at the University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston.
Non-small cell lung cancer is a major cause of cancer deaths in the United States, HemoCleanse said.

HemoCleanse made the announcement in conjunction with IDT Inc, a wholly owned subsidiary of Biocontrol Technology Inc of Pittsburgh. IDT has sponsored the hyperthermia treatment trials and holds exclusive worldwide marketing rights to the BioLogic-HT System and related disposables, HemoCleanse said.

The companies also said the BioLogic-HT System is being used in FDA-approved studies of whole-body hyperthermia in the treatment of HIV. Preliminary results suggest WBH may help extend the therapeutic effectiveness of drug therapties for patients in whom multi-drug therapies have been ineffective.
